original_question: Which disease is caused by a reactivated polyomavirus that destroys oligodendrocytes?

final_qi.question: Which disease is caused by a reactivated polyomavirus that destroys oligodendrocytes?
final_qi.long_answer: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) results from reactivation of the JC polyomavirus in immunocompromised individuals. The virus infects and lyses oligodendrocytes—the myelin-producing cells of the central nervous system—leading to multifocal areas of demyelination, hence the neurological deficits characteristic of the disease.

0.question: Which polyomavirus can reactivate and destroy oligodendrocytes?

final_answer.long_answer: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) arises when latent JC polyomavirus is reactivated, typically in immunocompromised individuals. The virus selectively infects and lyses oligodendrocytes, the myelin-producing glial cells of the central nervous system, leading to widespread demyelination and the characteristic multifocal white-matter lesions of the disease.
